agentic_risk_factors.description: The technical complexity of agentic systems, which can orchestrate numerous AI agents each powered by a "black box" AI model, can make it harder to interpret their behaviours and decisions.

source.section: Select New Challenges and Potential Risks of Agentic AI
source.quote: The technical complexity of agentic systems – which can orchestrate numerous AI agents

agentic_risk_factors.description: Alignment with human intentions is a well-known existing challenge for AI; the complexity of agentic architectures and their use for more complex tasks over longer time horizons makes alignment more challenging.

source.section: Select New Challenges and Potential Risks of Agentic AI
source.quote: Alignment with human intentions is a well-known existing challenge for AI.

agentic_risk_factors.description: Complex interactions between components, especially between different agents, are difficult to predict; even where individual agents behave within acceptable parameters, emergent behaviours could lead to unintended or undesirable outputs.

source.section: Select New Challenges and Potential Risks of Agentic AI
source.quote: emergent behaviours from systems of individually performant agents could lead to unintended or undesirable outputs

agentic_risk_factors.description: In complex agentic systems, especially those with multiple interconnected agents, the number of points of failure increases non-linearly, and errors in one agent or component could cause unpredictable or unwanted behaviour overall.

source.section: Select New Challenges and Potential Risks of Agentic AI
source.quote: the number of points of failure increases non-linearly

agentic_risk_factors.description: Agentic systems are characterised by high levels of autonomy, including the ability to take actions that impact the digital and physical environment (such as executing actions in other software); high degrees of autonomy pose increased risks of unintended harms.

source.section: Select New Challenges and Potential Risks of Agentic AI
source.quote: Agentic systems with high degrees of autonomy pose increased risks of unintended harms.

agentic_risk_factors.description: Agentic systems frequently interact with other services or the open internet and collect large quantities of user and enterprise data; data replication between components and the large attack surface of interconnected systems enhances the risk of intrusions or privacy violations, and autonomous action enhances the risk of hijacking by malicious actors without detection.

source.section: Select New Challenges and Potential Risks of Agentic AI
source.quote: the large attack surface of highly interconnected systems, enhances the risk of intrusions or privacy violations

agentic_risk_factors.description: Agentic AI, especially systems with extensive user-managed components, may create new challenges around identifying ownership and assigning responsibility for impacts.

source.section: Select New Challenges and Potential Risks of Agentic AI
source.quote: may create new challenges around identifying ownership and assigning responsibility for impacts

agentic_risk_factors.description: The additional complexity and many interconnected components make it harder to comprehensively identify risks or test behaviours, and make root cause analysis after incidents more difficult.

source.section: Select New Challenges and Potential Risks of Agentic AI
source.quote: root cause analysis is made more difficult by the number of independent components in the system

agentic_risk_factors.description: Agentic AI can increase the number of individual AI models and systems in an FI's ecosystem; without enabling infrastructure and a robust, scalable, automated governance framework, effective long-term oversight is challenging.

source.section: Select New Challenges and Potential Risks of Agentic AI
source.quote: FIs may find it challenging to effectively oversee Agentic AI over the long term

agentic_risk_factors.factor: Inbound risks from customer AI agents
agentic_risk_factors.description: Beyond the Handbook's scope, general adoption and acceleration of Agentic AI can introduce further inbound risks, such as when customers use AI agents to interact with an FI.

source.section: Select New Challenges and Potential Risks of Agentic AI
source.quote: such as those introduces when customers use AI agents to interact with an FI

agentic_risk_factors.factor: Complexity or "agenticness" as a risk assessment factor
agentic_risk_factors.description: FIs can weight complexity or "agenticness" as a factor in risk assessments; more complex systems can require more extensive controls.

source.quote: weight complexity or "agenticness" as a factor in their risk assessments

agentic_risk_factors.description: Security challenges include injections into shared memory functions, attacks on data in transit between agents, and denial-of-service-style attacks introducing infinite loops between agents.

source.quote: injections into shared memory functions, attacks on data in transit between agents

data.accountability_principle: In general, it is most effective to assign final accountability for an AI agent's actions to the party that had the most control over that action – creating an effective incentive to use that degree of control to ensure that the agentic system behaves as intended.

accountability_source.quote: it is most effective to assign final accountability for an AI agent's actions to the party that had the most control over that action

never_delegate_examples.why: Some actions may be too risky to delegate to AI under any circumstances.

source.quote: some actions may be too risky to delegate to AI under any circumstances, such as authorising financial transactions

never_delegate_examples.why: Some actions may be too risky to delegate to AI under any circumstances.

source.quote: too risky to delegate to AI under any circumstances, such as authorising financial transactions or making employment decisions

interruption_controls.control: Least privilege / restricted tool and data access
interruption_controls.description: Restricting privileges, tool and data access, and capabilities of an agentic system; giving agentic systems the lowest possible level of privilege for their use case and making privileges more restrictive for individual components, such as allowing only one specialised agent to access sensitive data or the internet.

source.quote: giving agentic systems the lowest possible level of privilege for their use case

interruption_controls.control: Secure-by-design screening and frequent session resets
interruption_controls.description: Robust screening of inbound data and of data handed off between agents, with frequent resets of agent sessions, to counter risk vectors such as agents receiving malicious instructions from the internet.

source.quote: robust screening of inbound data, data handed off between agents, and with frequent resets of agent sessions

interruption_controls.description: Restrictive, carefully designed data access limits on agents to mitigate malicious attacks or data leakages, plus minimising data that interacts with the agentic system.

source.quote: Restrictive, carefully designed data access limits on agents can mitigate against malicious attacks or data leakages.

interruption_controls.control: Grounding instructions to avoid certain actions
interruption_controls.description: Grounding AI agents with useful context, such as intended purpose or instructions to avoid certain types of action (such as spending money) unless specifically prompted.

source.quote: they should avoid certain types of action (such as spending money) unless specifically prompted to do so

interruption_controls.description: Robust and searchable logging and the capability to trace erroneous or harmful outputs back through the system to their initial point of failure.

source.quote: robust and searchable logging and the capability to trace erroneous or harmful outputs back

interruption_controls.control: Kill switches and other forms of "interruption"
interruption_controls.description: Used, proportionate to risk materiality, to stop Agentic AI systems that could take unintended or harmful actions such as spending money, issuing communications, or other hard-to-reverse behaviours; can be given to individual users or automated so harmful actions are promptly identified and blocked.

source.quote: Kill switches and other forms of "interruption" can be especially useful, if proportionate to risk materiality

interruption_controls.description: A prominent interruption feature that pauses or restarts agents that have been running for an extended period of time, to limit expense and improve alignment on complex tasks.

source.quote: "timeouts", which pause or restart agents that have been running for an extended period of time

interruption_controls.description: Limited initial rollouts enable FIs to identify emergent behaviours and other complex failure modes that testing may not uncover.

source.quote: Phased rollouts and pilot deployments are particularly useful when using Agentic AI

interruption_controls.description: Automated monitoring, or monitoring performed by dedicated AI agents, for unexpected behaviours; the monitoring agent itself must be robustly tested. Includes monitoring data ingress/egress for prompt injection or data leakage and monitoring usage of connected tools for anomalous activity.

source.quote: FIs can consider the value of automated monitoring, or even monitoring performed by dedicated AI agents

interruption_controls.description: Human-in-the-loop review as a guardrail for certain types of risky actions, with distributed approvals (such as by employees operating the agent) to make human review practical at scale.

source.quote: FIs can consider distributed approvals (such as by employees operating the agent)

tool_access_risks.description: Tool access is one of the most important vectors of risk for agentic systems; the potential impact of connected tools is a key consideration in determining the riskiness of an Agentic AI use case.

source.section: Select New Challenges and Potential Risks of Agentic AI
source.quote: Tool access is one of the most important vectors of risk for agentic systems

tool_access_risks.factor: Internet and external service interaction / attack surface
tool_access_risks.description: Agentic systems frequently interact with other services or the open internet and collect large quantities of user and enterprise data; replication of data between components and the large attack surface of highly interconnected systems enhances risk of intrusions or privacy violations.

source.section: Select New Challenges and Potential Risks of Agentic AI
source.quote: Agentic systems frequently interact with other services or the open internet

tool_access_risks.description: The ability of Agentic AI to take actions autonomously without a human's direct involvement enhances the risk of being hijacked by malicious actors to perform actions without detection.

source.section: Select New Challenges and Potential Risks of Agentic AI
source.quote: enhance their risk of being hijacked by malicious actors to perform actions without detection

tool_access_risks.factor: Potential attack surfaces, such as agents with internet access
tool_access_risks.description: Use case risk assessments should consider Agentic AI-specific factors, especially the tools the agentic system will have access to and the use case's potential attack surfaces, such as agents with internet access.

source.quote: the use case's potential attack surfaces, such as agents with internet access

tool_access_risks.factor: Malicious instructions received via internet access
tool_access_risks.description: A key risk vector is scenarios where an AI agent accesses the internet and receives malicious instructions; systems should be secure-by-design with screening of inbound data and data handed off between agents.

source.quote: scenarios where an AI agent accesses the internet and receives malicious instructions

tool_access_risks.description: When assessing data risks, FIs can consider whether sensitive information could be passed between agents in a multi-agent system, risking leakage.

source.quote: whether sensitive information could be passed between agents in a multi-agent system

tool_access_risks.description: Tools connected to agentic systems that experience anomalous or inappropriate usage, such as spikes in activity or attempts to access sensitive data, can indicate an agentic system is compromised or malfunctioning.

source.quote: Tools that experience anomalous or inappropriate usage, such as spikes in activity

gen_ai_vs_agentic.gen_ai: Gen AI systems like RAG-based chatbots are not typically referred to as Agentic AI due to their relatively low levels of autonomy.
gen_ai_vs_agentic.agentic_ai: Agentic AI describes systems that include components for making plans and for taking action, often involving tools that interact with their environment.

source.section: Characteristics of Agentic AI
source.quote: Gen AI systems like RAG-based chatbots are not typically referred to as Agentic AI due to their relatively low levels of autonomy.

gen_ai_vs_agentic.gen_ai: Non-Agentic AI: Gen AI with Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) – an LLM chatbot with basic retrieval capabilities from a static knowledge base (user prompt/response, search/summary of knowledge base).
gen_ai_vs_agentic.agentic_ai: Agentic AI: a single agent with reasoning capability (LLM-based agent with reasoning and structured actions, using internal workflows for planning, action, memory and tools), and multiple agents collaborating and delegating (a generalist agent orchestrating specialist, supervisor and learning agents for end-to-end automation); characterised by more autonomy, more planning, more independent action and more complex capabilities.

source.section: Figure 5.0.1
source.quote: Figure 5.0.1: Stylised Comparison of Gen AI and Agentic AI Architectures

gen_ai_vs_agentic.gen_ai: Gen AI was primarily constrained to content creation, summary, or retrieval tasks.
gen_ai_vs_agentic.agentic_ai: Agentic AI can take complex, multi-step actions, creating plans from high-level natural language directions and executing them using connected tools; it can undertake tasks that could never before be automated, representing a substantial maturation of Gen AI.

source.section: Business Potential of Agentic AI
source.quote: a substantial maturation of Gen AI, which was primarily constrained to content creation, summary, or retrieval tasks

gen_ai_vs_agentic.gen_ai: Gen AI systems were primarily reactive in nature, relying on users to take actions on their advice.
gen_ai_vs_agentic.agentic_ai: Agentic systems have the potential to be proactive, to effect real-world states directly, and to offload tasks not well-suited to AI to other software tools (e.g. passing mathematical tasks to a traditional calculator).

source.section: Business Potential of Agentic AI
source.quote: Where Gen AI systems were primarily reactive in nature, agentic systems have the potential to be proactive

gen_ai_vs_agentic.gen_ai: Losing context on broader and more complex tasks is a major limiting factor for LLM utility.
gen_ai_vs_agentic.agentic_ai: Agentic systems can, through their memory and planning functions, take on broader and more complex tasks without losing context.

source.section: Business Potential of Agentic AI
source.quote: take on broader and more complex tasks without losing context, which is otherwise a major limiting factor for LLM utility

gen_ai_vs_agentic.gen_ai: A known challenge in business adoption of Gen AI is its tendency to commit errors or outright hallucinate information, which can make it risky for critical use cases.
gen_ai_vs_agentic.agentic_ai: While errors and hallucinations also occur, multi-step reasoning processes or built-in error checking give agentic systems greater potential to catch their own errors, and their multiple steps and components lend themselves to guardrail modules (PII screening, toxicity detection, fact-checking).

source.section: Business Potential of Agentic AI
source.quote: the introduction of multi-step reasoning processes or built-in error checking gives agentic systems a greater potential to identify and catch their own errors

gen_ai_vs_agentic.aspect: Materiality/complexity of workflows suited to the technology
gen_ai_vs_agentic.gen_ai: Prior AI architectures could tackle less complex, lower-materiality workflows.
gen_ai_vs_agentic.agentic_ai: Agentic systems are currently well-suited to tackling more complex, higher-materiality workflows than prior AI architectures could.

source.section: Business Potential of Agentic AI
source.quote: well-suited to tackling more complex, higher-materiality workflows than prior AI architectures could

gen_ai_vs_agentic.gen_ai: Traditional model validation focused on the model.
gen_ai_vs_agentic.agentic_ai: Agentic AI accelerates a shift away from traditional model validation towards assessments of systems in the context of their use cases, because challenges arise in interactions between components and between agents.

source.quote: Agentic AI accelerates a shift away from traditional model validation and towards assessments of systems in the context of their use cases.

gen_ai_vs_agentic.agentic_ai: Agentic AI increases the importance of dynamic data governance focused on real-time oversight of how agentic systems access and use data.
